title: hierarchical-burst-slicing-and-utilization-ledger
author: Asha Nair
description: Summary: Introduces a hierarchical burst-slicing allocator for Dedicated fleets plus a compact, traceable utilization ledger for sampled per-pool/tenant telemetry. Motivation: existing global burst-credit banks make it hard to reason about short-duration microbursts and to link burst consumption back to observed utilization patterns. This PR implements time-sliced burst allocations (slices) that are bounded, traceable, and reclaimable, and a utilization ledger that stores sampled utilization footprints using a compact rollup encoding. Changes: 1) allocator/burst/slicer.go: new HierarchicalSliceAllocator with two layers: global tranche manager and per-tenant slice queues. Slices are fixed-duration tokens (configurable, default 250ms) that can be reserved or borrowed with soft preemption. 2) allocator/ledger/ledger.go: the UtilizationLedger records reservoir-sampled utilization events with metadata {pool,tenant,seq,window_ms,version} and supports rollup windows to compress older samples. 3) controlplane/api/v1/dedicated_config.proto: adds knobs slice_size_ms, slice_retention_ms, ledger_rollup_ms, proactive_reclaim_threshold. 4) console/telemetry: dashboard template and query helpers that join ledger samples to burst allocations so operators can trace a slice to the serving node and request IDs. 5) tests: unit tests for slice allocation fairness, race-condition tests for slice reclamation, integration scenario that simulates short bursty tenants and verifies SLA preservation. 6) tooling: new CLI command redwoodctl ledger dump --pool <pool> --from <ts> that produces a compact CSV of samples for offline analysis. Backwards compatibility: allocator defaults to behavior equivalent to prior global-bank when slice_size_ms is set to 0; ledger uses sampling by default and does not require schema migration for existing metrics. Migration: small DB migration to create ledger_index table for accelerated queries. Config knobs/ defaults documented in release notes. Commits: "init hierarchical slice allocator and ledger stubs"; "implement tranche manager and borrowing semantics"; "add proto fields and console queries"; "ledger rollup encoding and storage adapter"; "add unit/integration tests and redwoodctl dump"; "fix race in overlap window and add comments". Files changed (high level): allocator/burst/slicer.go, allocator/burst/slicer_test.go, allocator/ledger/ledger.go, allocator/ledger/storage_sql.go, controlplane/api/v1/dedicated_config.proto, console/telemetry/ledger_dashboard.md, tools/redwoodctl/ledger_dump.go. Review notes and conversation: Diego: "I'm concerned about the race path when a slice is being reclaimed while the serving runtime is refreshing KV cache; can we add a strong ordering or a compare-and-swap on slice metadata?" Asha (author): "Good catch; I added an atomic CAS on slice state and a short grace window to avoid preempting an in-flight KV refresh; see allocator/burst/slicer.go line ~214 for CAS usage and a unit test that reproduces prior flakiness." Priya: "The rollup encoding is clever but it's hard to interpret for operators; can we include a translation helper and an example in the console docs?" Asha: "Added console/telemetry/ledger_dashboard.md with example queries and a small translation helper in tools/redwoodctl/ledger_decode." Owen: "Please ensure the new proto fields are optional and added behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers upgrading older control planes." Asha: "Fields are optional and the control plane honors slice_size_ms=0 as legacy path; updated proto and added a note in controlplane/README." CI summary: initial run failed lint due to formatting in ledger.go; formatting fixed in second commit; unit test slice_reclaim_race was flaky on first run due to timing assumptions - replaced with deterministic simulation harness and test stabilized. Integration e2e simulated 200 tenants with synthetic microbursts and verified 99th percentile latency remained within SLO for reserved tenants while non-reserved tenants experienced controlled soft-throttles. Rollout plan: feature-gate default off for auto-rotation; opt-in via account-level DedicatedConfig.slice_enabled=true for initial ramp. Observability: new metrics exposed: redwood_dedicated_slice_allocated_total (counter), redwood_slice_reclaims_total (counter), redwood_utilization_ledger_samples_total (counter), redwood_utilization_ledger_rollup_version (gauge). Console adds a pre-built dashboard and a tracing join to link slice_id to request ids. Performance notes: allocator introduces a small constant CPU overhead in control plane (~2-4% at 1k qps) measured in bench harness; benefits in tail-latency and cost isolation shown in benchmark lab run 2026-01-15. Security/Compliance: ledger may contain tenant identifiers; sampling and retention respect tenant data-export settings and ledger storage honors KMS encryption at rest. Documentation: updated controlplane/README, console/telemetry README, and added an operator-runbook for debugging slice contention. Release notes: Provided below. Merge outcome: approved by reviewers Diego and Priya after addressing CAS race and doc additions; CI green; merged by squash on 2026-02-06. Linked work: ENG-5421 design doc, ENG-5489 telemetry spike.

release_notes: - Add hierarchical burst slice allocator for Dedicated fleets: time-sliced, bounded burst tokens with soft preemption and reclaimability. - Introduce Utilization Ledger: reservoir-sampled, rollup-compressed per-pool/tenant utilization records with console join support. - New control-plane knobs: slice_size_ms, slice_retention_ms, ledger_rollup_ms, proactive_reclaim_threshold (optional, backward compatible). - New redwoodctl ledger dump and decode helpers for offline analysis. - Observability: metrics and dashboard templates for tracing slices to requests. - Rollout: feature-gated; opt-in per-account for initial ramp.
